newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares seen flat to higher through Friday.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares seen flat to higher through Friday.

text.p: Belgian shares, which rose to new records on Tuesday, should remain well supported for the rest of this week though may find it hard to move significantly higher, dealers said.
"It could be a little tense before (U.S.) non-farm payrolls on Friday, but maybe after we can go higher again," one said.

Another said the Bel-20 leading share index would need to consolidate its close on Tuesday above resistance at 2,150 points to create a technical platform for further gains. "It looks positive, but we have to stay here for a few days," he said.
Oil and gas group PetroFina, steel maker were all helped higher by recent brokerage "buy" recommendations.

Electronics company Barco missed the boat, however. One trader said some analysts had turned neutral to negative on the share which has posted strong growth in the past two years. "The company itself talks about earnings per share growth of 10 to 15 percent. For this kind of stock that's not much," one said.

An overnight break by the dollar over 1.70 marks/35 francs and firmer bonds pushed the Bel-20 Index .BFX to record levels on Tuesday, but after an initial surge at the open the index was stuck in a range for most of the session.
The Index ended up 15.64 points, or 0.73 percent, at a new closing high of 2,158.07, just a shade below a new all-time high of 2,159.88 also set on Tuesday. The range was 2,155.93/59.88.
Banks were among the strongest gainers, with BBL up 240 francs, 3.13 percent, at 7,920 francs ahead of the release late on Wednesday of 1996 results. One trader said the share now looked expensive.
Dexia CC also continued its recent strong performance, rising 105 francs, or 2.88 percent, to 3,750 francs in active trade of 61,701 shares.
One trader said the stock was still being animated by the issue two week ago by Morgan Stanley of call warrants on the share. "They are still having to hedge," he said.

Non-ferrous metals company Union Miniere continued to benefit from the stronger dollar, which contributes around 500 million francs to its bottom line per Belgian franc rise. The share closed up 70 at 2,630 francs and one trader said it could rise as high as 2,900/3,000 in the near term.
